title: pacing-eddy-telemetry-sketch
content:
Purpose: quick exploratory notes for a lightweight pacing layer ("eddy" concept) to reduce short-term KV-cache thrash and smooth tail latency during microbursts. Not a polished runbook — thinking-out-loud telemetry + measurement log for follow-up experiments.

Hypothesis: inserting a tiny randomized pacing delay (2–12ms window) at ingress for requests that would otherwise be coalesced into very short inter-arrival gaps reduces expensive token-level cache evictions and lowers p95/p99 for small inference requests (<= 64 tokens) without harming throughput.

Cluster / env:
- cluster: ed-dev-3 (4x A10G, 32GB each, dev GPU pool)
- runtime image: serving-runtime:v2.9.1-experimental
- model: redwood-7b-1.4-q4_0 (local quantized build)
- test harness: bench-runner v0.12 (synthetic arrival generator), trace-collector v0.8

Traffic pattern used:
- baseline: Poisson qps target 120, with 3x microbursts (duration 6s) every 5m -> simulates small rapid fanout from frontend
- payload: 90% short (<=64 tokens), 10% medium (128–256 tokens)
- concurrency ceiling: 48 workers

Ingress pacing config (eddy):
- enabled for requests with token_estimate <= 64
- delay sampled uniform(2ms, 12ms) — jitter to avoid synchronized bursts
- cooldown window: 30s per connection (avoid double-pacing)
- bypass if queue_depth > 16 (don't add delay under heavy queuing)

Metrics collected (what I glued into trace-collector):
- per-request: arrival_ts, ingress_latency, queue_wait_ms, batch_size, tokens, kv_cache_hit, model_latency_ms, total_wall_ms
- per-gpu: gpu_util_pct, mem_used_mb, active_contexts

Run 1 — baseline (no eddy): 2026-02-26T09:12
- aggregate: avg_qps ~118 (target 120), sustained for 20m
- p50 model latency: 42ms, p95: 162ms, p99: 1185ms
- total p99 (wall): 1358ms
- KV cache hit rate (short reqs): 68%
- observed pattern: p99 spikes coincide with microburst windows; trace shows frequent cache evictions when bursts occur within 10–30ms spacing

Run 2 — eddy enabled (uniform 2–12ms): 2026-02-26T10:05
- avg_qps ~117 (within noise)
- p50 model latency: 44ms (slightly higher)
- p95: 138ms (improved ~15%)
- p99: 880ms (improved ~26%)
- total p99 (wall): 1020ms (improved ~25%)
- KV cache hit rate (short reqs): 82% (big jump)
- GPU util: stable, dropped 3–4% during bursts (less thrash)
- batch_size distribution: slightly more stable; percent of 1-request batches dropped from 34% -> 22%

Quick observations:
- Small added ingress jitter reduces pathological quick succession arrivals that previously forced tiny batches, which appears to correlate with fewer cache evictions.
- Throughput unchanged; overall GPU efficiency slightly improved (fewer context switches).
- Model-level p50 increased a touch (42 -> 44ms) — expected due to added delay but net user-facing p99 improved.
- Under heavier ceilings (concurrency > 64) the bypass rule matters — if we kept pacing when queue_depth was high, we started to see throughput impact.

Anomalies / weirdness:
- One microburst window showed a transient regression in p99- still investigating (2026-02-26T10:17). Trace shows an unrelated eviction from a medium-length request (128 tokens) that forced compaction; might be a separate GC-like event in cache implementation.
- A minority (~1.2%) of short requests had ingress delay > 20ms in traces; looks like sampling jitter + one misbehaving proxy introducing extra queueing.

Quick graphs I sketched (exported to trace-collector but not attached here):
- heatmap: inter-arrival vs. post-ingress batch size (clear vertical band of very small spacing dominating 1-batches in baseline)
- cdf: wall latency baseline vs eddy (left shift at p95, p99)
- time series: kv_cache_hit% vs p99 over 30m windows (strong inverse correlation)

Micro-bench follow-ups (next runs):
- A: sweep delay window: test uniform(0.5ms-6ms), (1ms-8ms), (5ms-20ms) — find knee where p50 cost outweighs p99 gain
- B: alternate distribution: exponential backoff sampling rather than uniform (to favor tiny delays most of the time)
- C: test without cooldown window to validate cooldown efficacy for long-tailed clients
- D: replicate on dedicated hardware (dedicated-asia-east-1-small) to rule out dev-cluster artifacts
- E: add explicit KV-cache instrumentation to record evict triggers + victim sizes (we only sample hit% right now)

Risks / UX notes:
- Added client-facing latency is visible at p50 — communicate tradeoff if rolled out (but net UX for tail-sensitive flows likely better).
- Need opt-out knob per-tenant (SLA customers), or a tiered policy (only for "best-effort" requests).

Action items (short):
- @Maya: can you wire the explicit eviction traces into trace-collector? small PR pref: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1299
- @Ibrahim: run A/B sweep A and B on ded-asia next week, collect 3x 20m windows each. add a flag in bench-runner for delay-dist param.
- @Rowan: file a short RFC for a per-tenant pacing policy and add to rollout checklist (include opt-out controls).

Notes-to-self:
- If we can get consistent p99 gain for <=64 token traffic with <10ms avg added latency, this is an easy platform-level knob to ship behind a feature flag.
- Consider coupling with short-request batching heuristic: if multiple small requests queued within 25ms, prioritize coalescing over immediate dispatch (sibling idea to eddy).

Unresolved questions:
- What's the interaction with model kv-cache lifetime for multi-turn chat? Could pacing cause more misses for sessions that expect immediate continuation? Need chat workload test.
- Is the apparent eviction from medium-length reqs a symptom of overall cache capacity being sized too low vs contended client mix?

Raw artifact pointers (local):
- traces: /mnt/bench-artifacts/eddy/2026-02-26/run2-traces-20260226.tgz
- bench configs: /repos/bench-runner/configs/eddy-sweep.yaml

End of sketch. Will iterate into a cleaner bench report with graphs and a proposed rollout policy if follow-up runs are promising.
